MESSAGE
[For Shri Srinivasan Jayaram, Station Commander and all the
Members of the XXI Winter Team, ‘Maitri’, Antarctica]
I felicitate you and all the team members at the Indian 
Station ‘Maitri’  on the occasion of Antarctic Mid Winter 
Day. The National Antarctic Programme has been achieving 
continuous success on account of the diligent efforts made 
by you and your colleagues. I have no doubt that your sincere 
and fearless work in such harsh conditions will achieve 
fruition. The people of India admire the courage and  
determination shown by all of you.
I wish all of you a happy and successful stay in  
Antarctica and a safe return home.
New Delhi 
June 11,2004

Dear Shri Jayaram,
I hope this communication finds you and other team members in the best of 
health and spirits.
2. The memorable moments which myself and other members of the  
delegation spent at Antarctica would remain vivid in our memory for long, I  
compliment you and your team members for the excellent arrangements made at 
the Indian base at Maitri and onboard M.V. Emerald Sea.
3. The National Antarctic Programme owes its success to the devotion and  
courage displayed by you all. Your relentless efforts in pursuit of scientific  
knowledge in the harsh conditions of Antarctica will certainly keep India’s image 
bright and high in the international arena. The people of India admire your  
determination and grit.
4. In this connection, I would also like to place on record the appreciation of  
the flying skills and behaviour of Capt. Craig Rose, Senior Pilot and Mr. Bruce 
Towers, Pilot, the two helicopter pilots. It was amazing to see them flying the  
choppers in the hills and the hostile environment with such perfection.
5. Wishing you and your team members the best of luck and success in all  
your future endeavours.
With warm regards,
Shri Jayaram 
23r d  Expedition Leader 
Indian Antarctic Expedition 
C/o Director, Antarctic Division, 
Geological Survey of India, 
NH-VF, NHYFaridabad

FOREWORD
The icy continent of Antarctica, known for its inaccessibility, harsh climate and 
remoteness is a challenging place for accomplishing the scientific goals that the successive 
teams venturing into the unknown, set for themselves. Undoubtedly, Antarctica is the ideal 
laboratory to decipher and link the past with the present.
India has maintained its perceptible presence in Antarctica since 1981. Ever since, 
the National Centre for Antarctic & Ocean Research at Goa was entrusted with the task and 
declared as the nodal agency for launching these expeditions, the Antarctic Program has 
grown and gained from the strengths of its partners. Today most of the reputed laboratories 
of CSIR, DST and DRDO, Survey Organizations, NTs and leading Universities are involved with 
this national endeavour in some way or the other.
Each member, especially one who volunteers for wintering over, demonstrates 
immense grit and determination. !  am happy that the XXIII Expedition has come out with 
success under the leadership Shri. S. Jayaram, a professional geologist from Geological 
Survey of India. The present report is the outcome of the results of the scientific programs 
undertaken by the participating organizations through their scientists under his able 
leadership.
This Expedition will also be remembered for the fulfilment of the stupendous 
assignment given to the special Task Force under the leadership of Rasik Ravindra of 
Geological Survey of India, to identify the site for establishing a new Research Station of 
India. The site has since been cleared by ATCM and the work on construction of the station 
has already started.
My recent visit to Antarctica in December 2009 has made me appreciate personally, 
the difficult conditions in which scientists and logistic personnel perform.
I  congratulate the team for their achievements.

The Indian Antarctic Program has been successful in bringing into its fold, newer 
organizations and younger participants to revitalize this national endeavour. The XXIII 
Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica that sailed to the icy continent under the 
leadership of Shri. S. Jayaram of the Geological Survey of India had several “firsts” to its 
credit.
